criterion: Confirm eligible PI, actual courses/leads, Greg’s four-hour/week total envelope, separate TA/lead hours, distinct backup and full-term coverage. No cash budget; fund any necessary expenses only from a confirmed eligible grant.
evidence: Named owners, realistic hours log, separate support commitments and confirmed grant/allowable-cost evidence if paid resources are needed.
stop: Counting four hours per role, assuming grant award, missing backup, or unfunded necessary spending.

criterion: Complete campus AWS CPU component tests and free-resource GPU benchmarks; retain failures, correctness, measured memory/runtime, checkpoint/export results and workload scope. Reproduce representative GPU work on awarded ACCESS hardware before class.
evidence: Versioned workload/environment manifest, dataset checksums, dated result rows, actual GPU/account limits and target-resource comparison. No measurements recorded yet.
stop: Unmeasured GPU amounts, treating free quota as guaranteed classroom capacity, or assuming benchmark timings transfer unchanged to ACCESS.

criterion: Confirm ACCESS CPU/GPU allocation, separate resource exchanges, actual quotas/storage, course dates and project structure; campus AWS stays test-only. If CloudBank is selected, confirm service type, CPU/GPU availability and accounting.
evidence: Provider response and approved award/resource configuration, recorded privately.
stop: Assuming unspecified limits, general broker terms or automatic renewal.

criterion: Every approved student/staff test account authenticates; student A cannot read/write student B files or instructor grading areas; removal/revocation works.
evidence: Access matrix and dated test results; no passwords or roster identifiers in public reports.
stop: Access leakage, shared credentials or unverified removal.

criterion: Both complete representative assignments run on the approved CPU image from fresh workspaces; no paid account or GPU is required. Pin the approved environment and input checksums.
evidence: Clean-run outputs, environment manifest, resource measurements and a known-good baseline.
stop: Missing packages, memory failure, unapproved app or required GPU dependency.

criterion: With provider permission, rehearse 80 simultaneous students plus agreed staff use in three representative sessions. Proposed p95 login-to-workspace ≤5 minutes; no unresolved assignment-blocking launch failure.
evidence: Dated latency distribution, workspace success count, quota/usage forecast and provider-agreed concurrency.
stop: No permission/capacity evidence; peak spec exceeds awarded limits.

criterion: Edit, save, stop/restart and recover a notebook/data package; verify filesystem location and retention. Export and re-import it into the CPU fallback.
evidence: Saved-file checksums, restart/export receipt and fresh-environment reopen.
stop: Student work depends on an unsaved session or cannot be exported.

criterion: Distribute a versioned assignment, collect it, reconcile all test submissions, preserve student authorship and instructor judgment, and import/export a test grade receipt through the approved LMS workflow. If Classroom 50 is selected, verify Team/Enterprise organization eligibility, permissions, billing controls and an independent export; Codespaces and Actions quotas remain separate.
evidence: Submission manifest and grade reconciliation results in the approved institutional destination. Classroom 50 canary and quota/fallback records if selected; no additional Codespaces allocation assumed.
stop: A leaderboard/auto-score substitutes for the authoritative grade, or a missing receipt goes undetected.

criterion: Approve provider and backup data destinations, lawful/appropriate datasets, access roles and retention. Keep grades/rosters in the approved LMS/institutional systems; publish only aggregate results.
evidence: Approved data map, rights notes, retention schedule and service/accessibility review.
stop: Assuming research storage or this public site is approved for private student records.

criterion: Rehearse keyboard and screen-reader access, readable instructions and equivalent small-data CPU/offline activity; resolve barriers in essential workflows.
evidence: User/task review and course-lead sign-off, with accommodations and fallback instructions.
stop: An essential assessed activity is inaccessible without an equivalent route.

criterion: Make independent copies in approved destinations and restore onto a different host/environment. Proposed RPO ≤24 hours and RTO ≤one business day; measure both.
evidence: Restore logs, independent file checksums, recovery timing and backup-operator runbook rehearsal.
stop: No independent copy or unmeasured recovery; relying only on snapshots or cold archival retrieval.

criterion: Publish actual staffed help windows and escalation route; rehearse an outage with CPU/small-data fallback. Proposed first response within one staffed business day; do not promise 24/7 support. Keep actual Greg hours within four/week across all duties; reduce scope when demand exceeds coverage.
evidence: Coverage schedule, ticket routing, outage exercise and fallback delivery proof.
stop: Unfunded coverage, unreachable operator or missed class deadline without substitution.

when: Before start; execute near term end
criterion: Schedule alerts 60/30/14/7 days before expiry; decide continuation at least 30 days before. Rehearse learner/grade export, retention and deletion; verify closure on the approved dates.
evidence: End-of-term runbook, sample exports, provider confirmation of exit window and deletion/renewal decision.
stop: Relying on grace periods, unconfirmed education extension or archival deposits of private coursework.
